title: Liquid-Phase Transmission Electron Microscopy of Ruthenium Oxide Electrocatalysts
content: Liquid phase transmission electron microscopy (LP-TEM) is a powerful tool for visualizing the structural dynamics of materials in liquid at near-atomic resolution. It has recently been utilized to visualize the dynamics of materials used for energy conversions, including the degradation of platinum nanoparticles supported on carbon [1] and the restructuring of battery materials during cycling [2]. Recent work from the Moreno-Hernandez Laboratory has utilized the technique to observe dynamics and discover the presence of structural heterogeneity within electrocatalyst materials for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), a critical reaction for electrolyzer devices [3, 4]. Our further understanding of these atomic-scale processes is been limited by resolution throughout the etching trajectory of the nanocrystals.
